summary.headline: HLE Glascoat order book crossed INR1,000 crore to INR1,087.3 crore at Sept 30, 2026, up 51% YoY and 64% QoQ, led by a EUR20.56m Fehmarnbelt cladding order.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was about INR346.7 crore, up 15.3% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR39 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT of about INR16 crore (4.6% margin). H1 revenue rose 2% to INR647.4 crore, while H1 EBITDA fell 23% YoY to INR61.6 crore at a 9.5% margin. Management said demand improved through Q2, with the order book at a record, though revenue recognition lags order booking by two or more quarters because revenue is booked only on dispatch. Working capital days rose to 102 from 80 in FY26. Management reiterated its FY28 targets of INR2,000 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.metric: Filtration, drying and other equipment revenue (Q2)

segments.name: Filtration, drying and other equipment
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR102 crore, up 5.4% QoQ from INR96.8 crore. Analysts flagged weak YoY performance in this segment despite pharma order inflow; management attributed it to execution lag.

segments.name: Glass lined equipment (India)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR195.4 crore, up 24.2% YoY. Management cited about INR110 crore in H1 for Indian GLE at high single-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Heat transfer equipment (Kinam)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR48.8 crore, down 12.3% YoY against a large one-off oil and gas order last year, but up 362.3% QoQ. Management called the business lumpy until a track record builds, 12-18 months away.

segments.name: THALETEC / European operations
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue from THALETEC Germany about INR192 crore at EBITDA margin a little over 11.5%, versus about INR343 crore for the prior 12-month period (management said pro-rata this is up 12-13%). Omeras (now HLE Surface Technologies) turned EBITDA breakeven in H1, with about EUR8.5 million turnover and PBT marginally negative.

guidance_outlook: FY28 consolidated revenue target of INR2,000 crore reiterated as on track; management said it will come from existing products, new products and Omeras products to be made in India.
FY28 EBITDA margin target of 15% reiterated; management said it is a return to historical levels, with Kinam and filtration and drying each about 16%, Indian GLE mid-teens, and THALETEC 12-14%.
FY27 revenue guided at INR260-280 crore for Indian GLE, with execution concentrated in Q3 and Q4.
Indian GLE can return to 16-18% EBITDA margin at around INR300 crore revenue, versus a best year near INR300 crore at over 18%.

Omeras: EBITDA-positive scale estimated at EUR20 million revenue per annum; 25-30 million EUR could reach double-digit EBITDA margin. A new Omeras-technology plant in India is expected to be commissioned in about two quarters.
Heavy engineering plant at Adas near Anand: initial EBITDA margin 15-18%, mature margin about 22%; management said there is no revenue ceiling.
risks_watch: Revenue H2 requirement: H1 revenue INR647.4 crore vs INR2,000 crore FY28 target implies about 35% H2 growth, which management did not quantify.
Filtration and drying execution: segment lagged on YoY basis despite pharma order inflow; watch whether H2 converts orders.
Heat transfer (Kinam) revenue is lumpy and down 12.3% YoY; track whether new oil and gas orders arrive.
Omeras remains PBT-negative due to interest and depreciation; turnaround depends on ramp to about EUR20 million revenue.
Working capital days rose to 102 from 80; watch cash conversion.
Management said the company will consolidate and not pursue acquisitions unless a strategic fit arises; about INR350 crore debt on balance sheet.
Management said it would try to split revenue by standalone, THALETEC, Omeras and Kinam in future presentations.
European cost pressures and geopolitical-driven delivery deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand scenario across key geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Harsh Patel said India demand is optimistic with high demand in API and specialty chemicals, Europe is slightly subdued but not weak, and US demand is high.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Filtration and Drying lag YoY despite pharma order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Ganjwala said execution cycles of 4-7 months mean orders booked now convert to revenue 2-3 quarters later, and revenue is recognised only on dispatch; geopolitical delays also pushed some customer dispatches out by a month or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kinam trajectory for FY27 and FY28 after the large FY26 oil and gas order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the traditional chemicals, paints and API business is growing reasonably, while oil and gas orders will be lumpy for the first one or two orders and become a continuing business in about 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 15% EBITDA margin still achievable, and what is the path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stands by the target: Kinam about 16%, filtration and drying about 16%, Indian GLE mid-teens, THALETEC 12-14%, which weighted together gives 15%; Q2 consolidated EBITDA margin was about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore FY28 revenue target intact, and how will H2 reach it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target is on track, driven by existing products, new products, and Omeras products to be made in India; it declined to give quarterly or half-year numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Indian GLE margin and revenue path back to historical peak levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the best year was about INR300 crore revenue at over 18% EBITDA margin, and at around INR300 crore with current cost structure it expects 16-18%; FY27 revenue guided at INR260-280 crore with current visibility concentrated in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company dealing with European cost inflation for THALETEC and Omeras?
qa_highlights.answer: Aalap Patel said Europe's cost pressures are being offset by sourcing non-critical components from India, with customer acceptance improving as end users look for capex efficiency, but European plants will not be emptied in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions or use cash for debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Ganjwala said the focus is consolidation after the Omeras acquisition about a year ago; debt of about INR350 crore is manageable, and acquisitions would be considered only if a strategic fit of right size arises.

capex_capacity: New heavy engineering plant at Adas near Anand: equipment over 100-150 tons, up to 4.5-5 m diameter and 15-20 m length, aimed at energy, oil and gas, petrochemicals and renewables; initial EBITDA margin 15-18%, mature about 22%; management said no revenue ceiling.
New Omeras-technology plant in India expected to be commissioned in about two quarters, enabling manufacture of Omeras products in India.
Indian GLE FY27 revenue guided at INR260-280 crore, with execution concentrated in Q3 and Q4 from the current order book.
Omeras (now HLE Surface Technologies): new COO from a large American multinational, new CFO, enhanced design team and new sales staff across European geographies.
Management said European manufacturing will not be fully shifted to India; non-critical components to be sourced from India over the next couple of years.
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book INR1,087.3 crore at Sept 30, 2026 (vs INR662 crore at June 30, 2026); about INR425 crore net accretion in Q2 and about INR350 crore executed, implying gross Q2 order inflow near INR775 crore.

Fehmarnbelt tunnel cladding order of about EUR20.56 million via HLE Surface Technologies; excluding its roughly INR210-220 crore booked value, the order book is about INR875 crore, which management said is repeating business with no Kinam-type large order.
Demand: India described as optimistic with high demand in API and specialty chemicals; Europe slightly subdued; US demand high.
Competitive intensity eased as equipment makers filling capacity pulled back; management said orders are being booked at improving margins month on month.
THALETEC products about 22% of Indian glass-lined product business in Q2.
Omeras H1 turnover about EUR8.5 million with EBITDA breakeven and PBT marginally negative due to interest and depreciation.
THALETEC Germany H1 FY27 revenue about INR192 crore at EBITDA margin a little over 11.5%, vs about INR343 crore for the prior 12-month period (management said pro-rata up 12-13%).
Indian GLE H1 revenue about INR110 crore at high single-digit EBITDA margin.
Execution cycle 4-7 months; revenue recognised only on dispatch, and customer-deferred dispatches linked to geopolitical delays were a Q1-Q2 drag.
Realisation query: management said mix (size, complexity, THALETEC premium products) drives realisation, with better realisations expected in coming quarters.
key_quotes: As of September 30, 2026, the consolidated order book stood at INR1,087.3 crores, registering a growth of 51% year -on-year and 64% quarter -on-quarter compared to INR662 crores as of June 30, 2026.
So we only account for revenues only when the equipment has been dispatched to the customer.
To be very honest, 15% is not an improvement. It is something that we've historically achieved and we are just getting back to those numbers.
I think the management is driven by consolidation at this point of time.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order book, demand and the FY28 targets, which management repeatedly reaffirmed as on track. Cautious and somewhat evasive on quarter-level numbers, H2 revenue phasing, the Filtration and Drying YoY shortfall and the Kinam trajectory, which it deflected to general timelines.
